---
title: "Changing the wording without changing the instruction"
subtitle: "Separate a real rewrite from a meaning-preservation check"
description: "Learn how to generate paraphrases and examine names, numbers, negation, and modality without treating word overlap as equivalence."
categories: [natural language generation, paraphrasing, evaluation]
---

June edits public notices for an archive. Sentences with identical wording can seem unnatural.
However, a rewrite creates a new instruction if it changes who may enter or what
visitors must bring.

For this lesson, a **paraphrase** changes wording but preserves the notice's
participants, quantities, negation, limits, and obligations. Linguistic research
sometimes accepts approximate meaning. An operational notice needs a stricter
rule because readers may act on one word such as `may`, `must`, or `not`.

Paraphrasing primarily preserves meaning while changing wording. Summarization
primarily compresses or selects content. Simplification primarily reduces
complexity or makes the language less formal. An output can serve more than one
aim, so these classes can overlap.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What you will learn

This lesson shows how to:

- generate paraphrase candidates with a fixed local model
- keep an unchanged-input baseline beside the generated wording
- measure visible wording change without treating it as semantic equivalence
- examine names, numbers, negation, and modality
- preserve model failures instead of removing them
- record human checks of meaning as pending.
:::

## Load the same fixed checkpoint

This page uses the summarization lesson's checkpoint, or saved model. The task,
prompt, baseline, and rule for checks differ. `huggingfaceR` loads the model from the
prepared local directory.

```{r}

model_record <- paraphrase_model$metadata |>
  select(model_id, revision, license)
```

## Write the preservation rule first

The author constructed these four behavioral probes to expose common changes
in operational meaning. A **probe** is a selected diagnostic example. The probes
are not a random test set. The lesson calculates no population accuracy estimate
from them.

`protected_name`, `modality_class`, and `modality_pattern` are blank when a
probe does not need that check. The baseline uses a copy of the source.
Copying preserves the original wording and facts, but it does not perform the
requested rewrite.

```{r}
paraphrase_inputs <- tribble(
  ~probe_id, ~source_text, ~protected_name, ~requires_negation,
  ~modality_class, ~modality_pattern,
  "PAR-01",
  "The clinic sent 24 reminder letters on Monday.",
  "",
  FALSE,
  "",
  "",
  "PAR-02",
  "Visitors may bring one notebook to the reading room.",
  "",
  FALSE,
  "permission",
  "\\b(may|can|allowed|permitted)\\b",
  "PAR-03",
  paste(
    "Maya Chen did not cancel the 14 September workshop;",
    "she moved it from Room 2 to Room 5."
  ),
  "Maya Chen",
  TRUE,
  "",
  "",
  "PAR-04",
  "Only archive staff must sign the restricted-room log.",
  "",
  FALSE,
  "obligation",
  "\\b(must|required|obliged|has to)\\b"
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  paraphrase_inputs,
  col.names = c(
    "Probe ID",
    "Source notice",
    "Protected name",
    "Negation required",
    "Modality class",
    "Accepted surface markers"
  ),
  caption = "Constructed paraphrase probes and predeclared invariants",
  row.names = FALSE,
  format = "html"
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  identical(paraphrase_inputs$probe_id, paste0("PAR-0", 1:4)),
  !anyDuplicated(paraphrase_inputs$probe_id),
  identical(sum(paraphrase_inputs$requires_negation), 1L),
  identical(
    paraphrase_inputs$modality_class,
    c("", "permission", "", "obligation")
  )
)
```

## Generate candidates without silent truncation

The complete chat-formatted prompt must stay below 192 input tokens. Greedy
decoding selects the highest-scoring next token. This method and a 72-token
output limit make the call repeatable. Deterministic generation can still
produce an incorrect paraphrase.

```{r}
paraphrase_system <- paste(
  "Rewrite the notice in different words.",
  "Preserve every participant, quantity, date, negation, scope,",
  "permission, and obligation.",
  "Return the rewritten notice only."
)

paraphrase_requests <- paraphrase_inputs |>
  mutate(
    user_prompt = paste0(
      "PROBE ID: ", probe_id,
      "\nNOTICE: ", source_text
    ),
    model_prompt = map_chr(
      user_prompt,
      \(user) {
        nlg_chat_prompt(
          paraphrase_model$tokenizer,
          paraphrase_system,
          user
        )
      }
    ),
    input_tokens = map_int(
      model_prompt,
      \(prompt) nlg_token_count(paraphrase_model$tokenizer, prompt)
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  paraphrase_requests |>
    select(probe_id, input_tokens),
  col.names = c("Probe ID", "Complete prompt tokens"),
  caption = "The workflow examines paraphrase input counts before generation",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

nlg_assert_input_budget(
  paraphrase_requests$input_tokens,
  max_input_tokens = 192L,
  item_ids = paraphrase_requests$probe_id
)
stopifnot(all(paraphrase_requests$input_tokens > 0L))
```

Only after that assertion succeeds does the lesson make any generation call.

```{r}
paraphrase_results <- paraphrase_requests |>
  mutate(
    generation = map(
      model_prompt,
      \(prompt) {
        nlg_generate(
          paraphrase_model,
          prompt,
          max_new_tokens = 72L,
          repetition_penalty = 1.05
        )
      }
    ),
    candidate = map_chr(generation, "text"),
    candidate_display = str_replace_all(
      candidate,
      "\\s*\\n+\\s*",
      " / "
    ),
    output_tokens = map_int(generation, "output_tokens"),
    ended_by_eos = map_lgl(generation, "ended_by_eos"),
    hit_token_cap = map_lgl(generation, "hit_token_cap"),
    copy_baseline = source_text
  )
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  paraphrase_results |>
    select(probe_id, source_text, candidate_display, copy_baseline),
  col.names = c(
    "Probe ID",
    "Source",
    "Generated candidate",
    "Unchanged-input baseline"
  ),
  caption = "Generated paraphrases retain failures and copies for inspection",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  all(paraphrase_results$input_tokens <= 192L),
  all(nzchar(paraphrase_results$candidate)),
  all(paraphrase_results$output_tokens > 0L),
  all(paraphrase_results$output_tokens <= 72L),
  all(
    paraphrase_results$ended_by_eos |
      paraphrase_results$hit_token_cap
  ),
  any(paraphrase_results$candidate != paraphrase_results$source_text)
)
```

The copy baseline should pass every literal preservation check. It also fails
the user's request for different wording. Each generated candidate must preserve
meaning and change wording.

## Measure wording change

This diagnostic converts each string to lowercase. It extracts letter and
number sequences with the ICU regular-expression engine in `stringr`. It then
computes Jaccard overlap between the unique token sets. Jaccard overlap divides
the number of shared tokens by the number of tokens in either set. An overlap
of 1 means the sets match. A lower
value means some visible wording changed.

```{r}
token_set <- function(text) {
  str_extract_all(
    str_to_lower(text, locale = "en"),
    "[\\p{L}\\p{N}]+"
  )[[1]] |>
    unique()
}

jaccard_overlap <- function(left, right) {
  left_tokens <- token_set(left)
  right_tokens <- token_set(right)
  length(intersect(left_tokens, right_tokens)) /
    length(union(left_tokens, right_tokens))
}

wording_diagnostics <- paraphrase_results |>
  transmute(
    probe_id,
    exact_copy = candidate == source_text,
    unique_token_jaccard = map2_dbl(
      source_text,
      candidate,
      jaccard_overlap
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  wording_diagnostics,
  digits = 2,
  col.names = c(
    "Probe ID",
    "Exact copy",
    "Unique-token Jaccard overlap"
  ),
  caption = "Wording diagnostics do not decide whether meaning is unchanged",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  all(
    wording_diagnostics$unique_token_jaccard >= 0 &
      wording_diagnostics$unique_token_jaccard <= 1
  ),
  any(!wording_diagnostics$exact_copy)
)
```

A low overlap can result from a good synonym or a damaging change. A high overlap
can still occur after removal of `not`. The score describes token sets, not equivalence.

## Examine visible invariants

An **invariant** is information that a rewrite must preserve. The code searches
for exact Arabic numerals, the protected name, and an explicit negation marker.
It also searches for a short list of markers for the predeclared modality
class. **Modality** distinguishes permission, obligation, and related meanings.

These string checks find some preventable mistakes. They also reject some
valid alternatives: `24` may become `twenty-four`, and `must` may become `have to`.
A string-check result cannot establish whether the rewrite preserves meaning.

```{r}
extract_numbers <- function(text) {
  str_extract_all(text, "\\b\\d+\\b")[[1]] |>
    sort()
}

has_negation <- function(text) {
  str_detect(
    text,
    regex(
      "\\b(no|not|never|without|cannot|can't|didn't|did not)\\b",
      ignore_case = TRUE
    )
  )
}

invariant_checks <- paraphrase_results |>
  mutate(
    numbers_preserved = map2_lgl(
      source_text,
      candidate,
      \(source, output) {
        source_numbers <- extract_numbers(source)
        if (length(source_numbers) == 0L) {
          NA
        } else {
          identical(source_numbers, extract_numbers(output))
        }
      }
    ),
    name_present = map2_lgl(
      protected_name,
      candidate,
      \(name, output) {
        if (!nzchar(name)) {
          NA
        } else {
          str_detect(output, fixed(name))
        }
      }
    ),
    negation_visible = map2_lgl(
      requires_negation,
      candidate,
      \(required, output) {
        if (!required) NA else has_negation(output)
      }
    ),
    modal_visible = map2_lgl(
      modality_pattern,
      candidate,
      \(pattern, output) {
        if (!nzchar(pattern)) {
          NA
        } else {
          str_detect(
            output,
            regex(pattern, ignore_case = TRUE)
          )
        }
      }
    )
  ) |>
  select(
    probe_id,
    numbers_preserved,
    name_present,
    negation_visible,
    modal_visible
  )

invariant_check_display <- invariant_checks |>
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        numbers_preserved,
        name_present,
        negation_visible,
        modal_visible
      ),
      nlg_screen_label
    )
  )

screen_actions <- invariant_checks |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    applicable_screens = sum(!is.na(c_across(c(
      numbers_preserved,
      name_present,
      negation_visible,
      modal_visible
    )))),
    flagged_screens = sum(c_across(c(
      numbers_preserved,
      name_present,
      negation_visible,
      modal_visible
    )) %in% FALSE)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(probe_id, applicable_screens, flagged_screens)

paraphrase_actions <- wording_diagnostics |>
  left_join(screen_actions, by = "probe_id") |>
  mutate(
    action = case_when(
      exact_copy ~ "revise wording",
      flagged_screens > 0L ~ "hold for human meaning review",
      TRUE ~ "send to human meaning review"
    )
  ) |>
  select(probe_id, flagged_screens, action)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  invariant_check_display,
  col.names = c(
    "Probe ID",
    "Arabic-numeral screen",
    "Protected-name screen",
    "Negation screen",
    "Modality screen"
  ),
  caption = "Conservative automatic checks for predeclared paraphrase invariants",
  row.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  paraphrase_actions,
  col.names = c("Probe ID", "Screen flags", "Next action"),
  caption = "Marks from automatic checks select candidates for human checks of meaning",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  identical(invariant_checks$probe_id, paraphrase_inputs$probe_id),
  all(vapply(invariant_checks[-1], is.logical, logical(1))),
  identical(nrow(invariant_checks), 4L),
  any(paraphrase_actions$flagged_screens > 0L),
  all(is.na(
    invariant_checks$name_present[
      !nzchar(paraphrase_inputs$protected_name)
    ]
  )),
  all(is.na(
    invariant_checks$modal_visible[
      !nzchar(paraphrase_inputs$modality_pattern)
    ]
  ))
)
```

A table value of `held for human review` requires a human check. It does not prove a change
in meaning. In this render, comparison with the source shows that the stress
probe copies prompt labels and omits Room 2.

The obligation probe replaces `must sign` with `authorized to sign`, changing
obligation to permission. Its modality check also selects the row for
a human check. However, the finite pattern list can also reject equivalent wording.
The conclusion therefore depends on human comparison, not the automatic check.

## Record check status

The model completed generation, and the automatic checks completed their limited
tasks. Human approval remains pending.

```{r}
paraphrase_review <- tibble(
  review = c(
    "local model execution",
    "complete prompt within 192 tokens",
    "wording-change diagnostic",
    "surface invariant checks",
    "human checks of meaning preservation",
    "human prose checks"
  ),
  status = c(
    sprintf(
      "completed: %d candidates",
      sum(nzchar(paraphrase_results$candidate))
    ),
    sprintf(
      "within budget: %d/%d candidates",
      sum(paraphrase_results$input_tokens <= 192L),
      nrow(paraphrase_results)
    ),
    sprintf(
      "computed: %d/%d candidates changed wording",
      sum(!wording_diagnostics$exact_copy),
      nrow(wording_diagnostics)
    ),
    sprintf(
      "held: %d/%d candidates flagged",
      sum(paraphrase_actions$flagged_screens > 0L),
      nrow(paraphrase_actions)
    ),
    "pending",
    "pending"
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  paraphrase_review,
  col.names = c("Check stage", "Status"),
  caption = "A generated rewrite is not an approved paraphrase",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  !any(paraphrase_review$status == "passed"),
  identical(tail(paraphrase_review$status, 2L), c("pending", "pending"))
)
```

June can accept a candidate only after comparison with the notice under the
initial preservation rule. Generation, visible wording change, and invariant
flags supply evidence for human checks. None replaces those checks.

## What to remember

- A paraphrase changes wording while preserving the information that matters.
- Copying is a useful preservation baseline, but it is not a successful rewrite.
- Token overlap measures wording, not semantic equivalence.
- Examine names, numbers, negation, limits, permission, and obligation separately.
- Keep failed model outputs visible when they reveal an invariant violation.
- Record human checks of meaning and prose apart from automatic execution.
